title: ERC orders P1.99 billion Meralco refund
summary: The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has ordered Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) to return around P1.99 billion to its more than eight million customers over three months.

blocks.text: The refund translates to an average rate of P0.1536 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) and will appear on customers’ bills as a separate line item labeled “RAB Refund,” the ERC said, following its commission meeting on Nov. 26.
MANILA, Philippines — The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has ordered Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) to return around P1.99 billion to its more than eight million customers over three months.
Residential and small commercial customers, meanwhile, will receive a larger refund of P0.2611 per kWh or about P52 for typical households consuming 200 kWh a month.
Francis Saturnino Juan, ERC chairman and CEO, told The STAR yesterday the refund is expected to be credited to customers’ bills starting next month.

The refund stems from the ERC’s revaluing of Meralco’s regulatory asset base (RAB) and disallowing certain pension and employee benefit expenses, in compliance with a Supreme Court ruling arising from a petition filed by the National Association of Electricity Consumers for Reforms Inc.
The refund order comes as a timely relief for Meralco customers, who are grappling with high electricity rates amid rising fuel prices, a weaker peso and tight power supply conditions.
These factors have driven up generation charges, which cover the cost of electricity procured from suppliers and were the primary contributor to the increase in Meralco’s overall rate this month.

“By acting decisively and completing this case now, the commission ensures that the amount due to consumers is returned when they need it most and that the refund will help cushion the impact of these increases on their monthly bills,” Juan said.

Under its ruling, the Supreme Court directed the ERC to reassess the valuation of Meralco’s RAB and establish guidelines for determining whether expenses not directly and entirely related to its operations may be passed on to consumers, either wholly or partially.
While recognizing that pension costs are legitimate expenses, the court held that Meralco must substantiate the amounts it seeks to recover from consumers.
